note: The challenge reason judge, measured (31 Oct 2026, after the 12-judge panel: 'n = 1'). Each reason is a student's pick and why on a teacher's challenge, labelled before any run: holds = true when the reason applies the right principle, false when it is luck, the old idea, parroted words or empty of reasoning. reason_eval.escript asks Muse Spark (witness_challenge:judge/3) and counts false accepts (a reason that does not hold, accepted) and false rejects. Kinds: worked (the numbers worked through), explained (the principle applied in words with the numbers), rule_of_thumb (right pick, no principle), old_idea (the misconception), words_only (the rule named with no working shown: labelled not holding, reported on its own because a teacher may accept it).

water.diagnosis: takes the second change of the original amount
water.q: A town stores 1,000 litres of water. The supply falls by 30%, then rises by 30%. How much water is there now?

fractions.diagnosis: adds the tops and the bottoms
fractions.q: A recipe uses 1/3 cup of sugar and 1/6 cup of honey. How much sweetener in all?

density.q: A stone has a mass of 300 g and a volume of 120 cm^3. What is its density?

speed.diagnosis: averages the two speeds instead of total distance over total time
speed.q: A cyclist rides 20 km at 10 km/h and then 20 km at 20 km/h. What is the average speed?

reasons.why: 30% of 1000 is 300 so 700 left. Then 30% of 700 is 210, so 910.
The rise is taken of the new amount, which is smaller, so it ends lower: 700 x 1.3 = 910.
It always ends a bit lower so I picked the one under 1000.
Minus 30% then plus 30% cancels out.
